title: WPSS/985/2011 of SMT MANJU PANDEY and OTHERS Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
(1) Writ Petition No. 1841 of 2011 (S/S)
Rakesh Chand Bhatt and ors. ........Petitioners
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .......Respondents
WITH
(2) Writ Petition No. 1896 of 2011 (S/S)
Rishi Ram Raturi and ors. ........Petitioners
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .......Respondents

WITH
(3) Writ Petition No. 985 of 2011 (S/S)
Smt. Manju Pandey and ors. ........Petitioners
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .......Respondents
Mr. B.D. Uppadhyay, Senior Advocate with Mr. M.C. Pant, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. A.S. Rawat, Addl. Advocate General with Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for
the State.
Mr. V.B.S. Negi, Senior Advocate with Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the
intervener.
WITH
(4) Writ Petition No. 592 of 2012 (S/S)
Jawahar Singh Rathore and ors. ........Petitioners
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others. .......Respondents
Mr. B.S. Adhikarhi, Advocate for the petitioners.
Mr. A.S. Rawat, Addl. Advocate General with Mr. R.C. Arya, Standing Counsel for
the State.
Dated: May 29, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J.
 Controversy involved in all the petitions is
identical and this Court has to adhere and
adjudicate upon a common question of law,
therefore, common judgment is being passed in all
the petitions. Writ Petition No. 1841 of 2011 (S/S)
shall be the leading case.

2
2. This litigation commenced, when the Director
General of Police, Police Headquarter, Dehradun
started the promotional exercise for the post of
Inspector pursuant to the notification dated
19.04.2011 amongst the Sub-Inspectors, who have
completed 10 years of service upto 01.04.2010,
however vide notification dated 23.11.2010, the
Government relaxed the qualifying service of 10
years to 50% as one time measure.
3. It has been averred that petitioners have been
subjected to a hostile discrimination in the matter
of consideration of the candidature of the
petitioners in the process of promotion to the post of
Inspector from the post of Sub-Inspector, by taking
into consideration their appointment on the post of
Sub-Inspector w.e.f. 2008 when they completed
their training. Further, though the selection year to
the petitioner is granted in 1999, when the selection
process for promotional exercise of Sub-Inspector
was started. Apart from this, the petitioners were
selected by a common selection against the
vacancies of Sub-Inspectors arising out of year
1991-99. It is asserted that after bifurcation of
State, the vacancies existed upto November, 2000,
175 vacancies allocated to State of Uttarakhand for
the post of Sub-Inspector.
4. It is further stated that, the total 764 allocated
posts of Sub-Inspectors of the State of Uttarakhand
includes 175 posts in such vacancies, and if these
175 vacancies are not abolished by State of U.P.,

3
the same shall be sent to State of Uttarakhand. In
case, these 175 posts are abolished by State of U.P.
then only a list would have been sent to State of
Uttarakhand and those vacancies should have been
filled up amongst the employees, allotted to the
State of Uttarakhand. It is stated that petitioners'
promotion relates back to 1999 and accordingly,
they are entitled notional seniority w.e.f. 1999.
5. Contention of learned Senior Advocate for the
petitioners is that the petitioners are entitled for
grant of notional seniority from the year 1999, when
the process of promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector, from the post of Head Constables was
initiated and the petitioners were selected in said
promotion on the criteria of merit. Seniority to the
persons selected in the same selection, on the basis
of seniority, was provided from the year 1999, but
the petitioners have been deprived of the same.
Further, the respondents, after framing of the
Uttarakhand Police Act, could not have proceeded
on the basis of the Govt. Orders dated 23.09.2004
and 15.12.2006, which were issued under the Police
Act, 1861 {hereinafter referred to as the Act
(repealed in the State of Uttarakhand from
04.01.2008)} and no Govt. Order was issued under
the Uttarakhand Police Act, hence, in absence of
there being any condition of 10 years' service as
Sub-Inspector for considering the case of promotion
to the post of Inspector, in the Regulation, no such
condition could have been prescribed, without

4
issuing any Govt. Order under the Uttarakhand
Police Act.
6. Learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners
submitted that there is no such provision under
Regulation 437 of the Police Regulations, justifying
the condition regarding 10 years of service, and
admittedly it has been put under the Govt. Order
dated 23.09.2004 and 15.12.2006 and in view of
mandate of the provisions under the Uttarakhand
Police Act, the said Govt. Orders, issued under the
1861 Act, cannot be given effect to and the
respondents cannot proceed in the year 2011 on the
basis of such Govt. Orders, which have lost efficacy
and are no more in existence. He submits that as
evinced from Section 86 (2) of the Act, only the rules
and regulations, framed under the earlier Act, have
been saved to the extent of their operations till any
rules regulation framed and amended under the
Uttarakhand Police Act, but no such protection is
provided to the orders issued under the said Act
and the Legislature has deliberately issued the work
previous operation, which means that if any action
has been taken or initiated prior to the framing of
the Uttarakhand Police Act and, in that view of the
matter, the State Govt. could not have initiated
promotion process on the basis of the Govt. Orders.
He submits that as per the mandate of Section 88 of
the Act, the State Govt. was empowered to issue the
order for removing difficulties arise in giving effect
to the provisions of the Uttarakhand Police Act, but
that too could have been done only within the

5
period of three years from commencement of the Act
i.e. the order could have been issued only till
03.01.2011 and not thereafter, but the State Govt.
has not cared to issue any order and has proceeded
to rely upon the orders issued years before the
framing of the Uttarakhand Police Act and,
therefore, the putting condition of 10 years service
is a condition beyond jurisdiction and is not even
traceable under the Uttarakhand Police Act or the
Regulations applicable till now.
7. It is further argued that on 04.01.2008, the
Uttarakhand Police Act was enforced in the State
and after more than 3 years the respondents could
not have laid down a condition, which was neither
under the Regulations nor under the Govt. Orders
issued under the Uttarakhand Police Act, but was
only under the Act, which cease to apply in the
State on and from 04.01.2008, consequently the
process of promotion stood legally vitiated and the
condition of 10 years service is not supported by
any Legislative authority, nor even by any
administrative authority, as the Uttarakhand Police
Act does not permit the continuance of the Govt.
Orders issued under the Act and no Govt. Order
was issued under the Uttarakhand Police Act. He
submits that had the Act been continuing in the
State, the petitioners could not have any room of
argument regarding the source of power, but when,
admittedly, the Act is repealed in the State on
04.01.2008, the Govt. Order issued under the Act,
cannot be applied in the process of promotion

6
initiated in the year 2011 i.e. after more than 3
years of the Uttarakhand Police Act being enforced.
8. Learned Senior Advocate for the petitioners
then submitted that the petitioners were selected in
the selection year 1999, but the benefits has been
denied/withheld, however, the persons selected in
the same selection year and in the same process of
selection, on the basis of seniority, have been given
their seniority from the selection year 1999. He
submits that the petitioners, who were promoted on
merits, are being deprived of reckoning of their
seniority for the said selection year. He submits that
a person qualifying on merits stands on a better
footing than that of a candidate qualifying only on
the basis of seniority. It is further submitted that
when a person is given the notional promotion from
the retrospective date, the period of service shall be
calculated from the date of notional promotions by
presuming that the incumbent is working on the
feeder post, consequently, if the petitioners are
granted the notional promotion from the year 1999,
the petitioners would become eligible for promotion
on the post of Inspector from that of Sub-Inspector,
even under the Govt. Orders dated 23.09.2004 and
15.12.2006, which prescribes the condition of 10
years of service, which are wholly illegal and
without jurisdiction. Learned counsel for the
petitioners placed reliance on the judgment of Apex
Court in 'Amarjeet Singh and ors. vs. Devi Ratan
and ors', reported in (2010) 1 SCC 417, 'Union
Public Service Commission and anr. vs. A.K. Salim

7
and ors.', reported in 2008 (2) SCC (L&S) 1021,
'Ashok Kumar Srivastava and ors. vs. Ram Lal and
ors.', reported in 2008 (1) SCC (L&S) 575 and the
judgment of Division Bench of this Court rendered
in Writ Petition No. 284 of 2010 (SB) 'H.K.Upreti
and anr. vs. State and ors.' Learned Senior Advocate
prayed that respondents be directed to consider the
candidature of the petitioners for the post of
Inspector and allow them to participate by treating
their appointment on the post of Sub-Inspector
w.e.f. 1999 in their quota and as per their selection
year awarded to them and further to direct the
respondents to accord the benefit of notional
seniority to the petitioners w.e.f. 1989/1991 as
given to other incumbents in the erstwhile State of
U.P. and fix their seniority accordingly. He prayed
that in this light, the order dated 06.08.2011,
denying seniority to the petitioners, be quashed. He
also prayed that the order dated 19.04.2011 to the
effect by which relaxation given in the qualifying
service by quashed. Shri B.S. Adhikari, Advocate
adopted the argument of Shri B.D. Uppadhyay,
Senior Advocate.
9. Mr. A.S. Rawat, learned Addl. Advocate
General for the State, on the other hand, contended
that the petitioners were initially appointed as
Constables on different dates, sometime between
1983-89 and subsequently, they were promoted to
the next higher post of Head Constables between
the period 1998-2003. He submits that prior to the
promotion of the petitioners to the post of Head

8
Constable, on 08.03.1995, the respondents by way
of notification, as empowered under Clause (c) of
sub-section 2 of Section 46 of the Police Act, 1886,
issued Recruitment Rules to the post of Sub-Inspector and by way of Govt. Order, a provision
was made for 50% promotion by way of direct
recruitment and 50% by way of promotion from the
feeder cadre of Head Constable. In such notification,
a separate provision was also made that out of 50%
of the promotion quota, 25% promotions were to be
made on the basis of seniority subject to the
rejection of unfit. However, the notification was
withdrawn vide another order dated 19.05.1998
reverting back to the earlier rule of 50% promotion
by way of departmental promotion. There were
about 388 Head Constables, who had become
eligible as per the aforesaid rules in between the
period of 08.03.1995 and 19.05.1998 under 25%
quota on the basis of seniority and subject to
rejection of unfit and they were also getting
promotional pay scale, and those eligible senior
Head Constables approached the Allahabad High
court and sought the benefit of the rules existing
between the said period. The Allahabad High Court
allowed their petition and the same was upheld by
the Division Bench of Allahabad High Court in the
case, namely 'State of U.P. vs. Ranveer Singh'. He
submits that since the judgment in Special Appeal
no. 1372/1999 was never challenged by anyone, the
same had attained finality. However, the Division
Bench of Allahabad High Court made an
observation that since the matter was pending in

9
Court and some of the promotees till 08.05.1995
must have either been retired or died, therefore,
they must also be given notional seniority w.e.f. the
date when their other batch mates were promoted.
Now the petitioners seeking parity with above those
Head Constables, who were promoted on the basis
of seniority subject to rejection of unfit under the
then prevailing recruitment rules between the
period 08.03.1995 to 19.05.1998, which they are
not entitled.
10. Learned Addl. Advocate General contended
that it was for the first time on 23.01.1999 the State
Government (erstwhile State of U.P.) initiated the
recruitment process for the post of Sub-Inspector
and the total vacancy upto 31.12.1999 were
calculated and the same were calculated to be
around 2956 vacancies, out of which there were
about 1564 vacancies in the promotional quota, and
since 388 Head Constables have already been
promoted to the post of Sub-Inspector under the
promotion rules existing between 08.03.1995 to
19.05.1998, therefore, after deducting those 388
posts, the then State Government vide notification
dated 03.02.1999 issued an order for filling up the
said vacancies. The State Government, in order to
balance the quota of direct recruits and promotees,
further added 86 more posts vide an office order
dated 10.01.2000. He submits that on 27.02.1999,
in supersession of the earlier order dated
03.02.1999, the guidelines for the selection of Sub-Inspector under promotion quota were issued and

10
as per the said guidelines, the departmental
promotion examinations were to be conducted in
three different stages. The first being preliminary
written examination and PT/IT (Physical Test &
Infantry Test) and the same was held in December,
1999. All the petitioners have also appeared in the
examination and they have qualified the same.
Alongwith other qualified person, the petitioners
were also supposed to appear in the written
examination, which was fixed for 11.02.2000.
However, some of the candidates, who have not
qualified the examination, challenged the same
before Allahabad High Court and the said Court
vide order dated 10.03.2000 allowed the writ
petitions filed by those persons, who could not
qualify the written examination. However, the said
judgment was reversed in an appeal filed by the
State on 02.12.2004 and therefore, finally the main
examination was held on 25.12.2005 and the result
of the main examination was declared on
24.01.2006. Thereafter, in the months of May and
July, 2006 interviews were conducted and the result
of the selected candidates was declared on
11.11.2006.
11. He then submitted that all the writ petitioners
in the instant petitions were allocated on
03.05.2003 to State of Uttarakhand and were in the
service since then. As the State of Uttarakhand did
not have its own infrastructure for the examination
and training etc. the State of Uttarakhand
requested and sent a requisition to the State of U.P.

11
for the training of petitioners, 66 in numbers, to
impart the training to the petitioners in PTC,
Moradabad, which was to be conducted between the
period 06.03.2007 to 06.09.2007. The petitioners
had completed their training by 25.08.2008 and
were appointed to their respective districts in the
State of Uttarakhand. After the creation of State of
Uttarakhand, since there has been an acute scarcity
of the police personnel in the State, particularly on
the post of Sub-Inspectors, the State conducted a
recruitment drive for the post of Sub-Inspector
against the direct quota in the year 2002-03. As
there were various Police Stations, which were
headless and various posts of Inspectors were lying
vacant, the respondent/State, therefore, wanted to
fill up the vacancies of Inspector, hence vide
notification dated 23.09.2004 fixed the eligibility
condition for the promotion to the post of Inspector
from Sub-Inspector and categorically laid down that
the 10 years regular service as Sub-Inspector would
be required for the recruitment to the post of
Inspector and the same would be counted from 1st
April preceding the selection year and alongwith
qualifying years, the eligibility criteria also provided
for 10 years A.C.R. and no adverse entry for the
immediate previous 03 years. However, vide
notification dated 23.11.2010 the qualifying years of
10 years were relaxed by 50% as a qualifying service
as one-time measure. Subsequently, the aforesaid
relaxation was withdrawn vide order dated
19.08.2011 and making it again 10 years as

12
qualifying service for the promotion to the post of
Inspector from the post of Sub-Inspector.
12. Learned Addl. Advocate General submits that
since the State of Uttarakhand was having acute
shortages of Inspectors in its various Police
Stations, as such the State issued a notification on
19.04.2011 inviting applications for recruitment of
Inspector in a promotion quota from the post of
Sub-Inspector and the eligibility criteria, as was
fixed vide notification dated 23.09.2004 was fixed as
the criteria for promotion. As the petitioners were
promoted to the post of Sub-Inspector for the first
time in the year 2008, and were not being eligible
for appointment to the post of Inspector, filed the
instant writ petitions for seeking notional promotion
from the date when the process for promotion to the
post of Sub-Inspector was initiated, so that they
become eligible for the selection to the post of
Inspector.
13. Contending on merits learned Addl. Advocate
General submitted that the petitioners were for the
first time born in the cadre in 2008, and therefore,
they are not entitled for any notional seniority with
retrospective date, as claimed by them. He submits
that Regulation 448A of the U.P. Police Regulations
(as applicable in State of Uttarakhand), provides
that seniority of a Sub-Inspector would be counted
only from the date of passing the Sub-Inspector
Armed Police Course, not prior to that date.
Besides, the above categorical provision, it is a

13
settled principle of law that the seniority to a Govt.
employee cannot be given for any period to which he
was not even born in the cadre. He submits that the
contention of the petitioners that since they were
eligible to appear in the departmental examination
for the promotion to the post of Sub-Inspector
sometime in 23.01.1999 when the recruitment
process had started, and since it was not their fault
that the same examination could not be concluded
till the year 2008, and that was because of the long
drawn litigation before the Courts, therefore, they
were entitled for the seniority from the date of
initiation of departmental promotion. In this
Context, learned Addl. Advocate General for the
respondents submits that the Hon'ble Supreme
Court and the various High Courts in catena of
cases has settled the principle of retrospective
promotion and has categorically held that the
promotion or seniority cannot be given
retrospectively from a date when the employee was
not even born in the cadre.
14. Learned Addl. Advocate General for the
respondents also contended that the Hon'ble Apex
Court in its various judgments has also
categorically laid down the principle that the benefit
of the maxim [actus curiae neminem gravabit (act of
court shall prejudice no one)] cannot be avail by all
the litigants where there is a delay on account of the
Court cases.

14
15. Main argument of the learned Senior Advocate
for the petitioners is that the petitioners cannot be
punished for the pendency of writ petitions before
the Allahabad High Court. Though, it is true that
early disposal of the writ petitions by the Allahabad
High Court would have resulted in early promotion
of the petitioners and further entitlement for the
higher promotion, but no benefit can be given to the
petitioners due to the pendency of the writ petitions
as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2010) 1 SCC
417 Amarjeet Singh & others vs. Devi Ratan and
others. In the present case, though petitioners
qualified preliminary examination for promotion,
held in 1999, but written (main) examination could
not be held due to stay order of Allahabad High
Court. Main examination was held on 25.12.2005
and result thereof was declared on 24.01.2006.
Thereafter, in the months of May and July, 2006
interviews were conducted and result of selected
candidates was declared on 11.11.2006, petitioners
were sent for training and they completed their
training by 25.08.2008. In this background, the
claim of petitioners for seniority/notional promotion
from the year 1999 cannot be accepted. The
relevant regulation is very clear, which provides that
seniority of a Sub-Inspector would be counted from
the date of passing Sub-Inspector-Armed Police
Course. Since the minimum experience for
consideration on the post of Inspector is ten years,
and the petitioners have not gained that experience,
no direction can be issued to the respondents to
consider the candidature of the petitioners for the

15
post of Inspector. Similarly, no direction can be
issued to the respondents to grant notional seniority
to the petitioners from 1991 and treat them
appointed on the post of Sub-Inspector in the year
1999.
16. Another submission of learned Senior
Advocate for the petitioners that after framing of
Uttarakhand Police Act, the respondents could not
have proceeded on the basis of Govt. Order dated
23.09.2004 and 15.12.2006. This argument also
has no force, as there is nothing on record, which
could show that Uttarakhand Police Act provides
contrary to these rules.
17. Judgment cited by the learned Senior Advocate
for the petitioners do not help the petitioners. In
(2010) 1 SCC 417 'Amarjeet Singh & others vs. Devi
Ratan & Others, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has
held that retrospective promotion is permissible in
exceptional circumstances when there is some legal
impediment in making promotion, like intervention
by Court. Benefit of this judgment cannot be given
to the petitioners, as in the matter of petitioners,
due to stay order of Allahabad High Court, selection
process could not be completed in the year 1999
and was completed only in the year 2006. In 'Union
Public Service Commission vs. A.K. Salim and
others' (2008) 2 SCC (L & S) 1021, as cited by the
counsel for the petitioners, the CAT directed
consideration of respondent's case for induction to
Indian Forest Service against single vacancy of

16
2006, Government, however insisted for
consideration of all cases of all candidates for all the
three vacancies for the year 2006. Meanwhile,
respondents retired on 31.05.2007. Govt. allowed to
convene Selection Committee for all the vacancies,
as agreed to by all the parties, but in order to
protect respondent's interest, held, in the event of
respondent's selection, intervening period to be
regularized notionally. But, facts of the petitioners'
case are entirely different. Another judgment (2008)
1 SCC (L & S) 575 cited by the learned Senior
Advocate for the petitioners also does not apply in
the case of the petitioners.
18. All the writ petitions fail and are dismissed. No
order as to costs.

19. Let certified copy of the judgment be placed in
the connected petitions.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 29.05.2013
NCM:
